old_title: Chelsea v Luton LIVE: Team news and updates from Carabao Cup
new_title: Chelsea v Luton LIVE: Carabao Cup latest score as Enzo Fernandez absence explained
old_text:
Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first competitive game at Stamford Bridge as Luton Town arrive for a Carabao Cup second-round tie, with Leeds United awaiting the winners in the third round.
The Blues, with such squad depth available to Alonso, are set to ring the changes but it will be curious to see if Enzo Fernandez, still subject to transfer interest from Manchester City, features in the squad - and more curious still to see how home fans greet his presence.
Alonso watched Chelsea's attack dazzle in a thrilling 3-2 win at Fulham on Monday for his first Premier League win, with Cole Palmer starring. League One side Luton won 3-0 away to Gillingham in the opening round to set up a glamour tie and have claimed four points from their opening two games.
Follow live updates from Chelsea v Luton, below
Luton XI confirmed!
Here is how the visitors line up.
Keeley; Ashby, Odoffin, Johnston, Johnson; Benagr, Walsh; Palmer, Lawrence, Kodua; Marshall.
Subs: Shea, Naismith, Andersen, Richards, Wells, Fox, Jones, Chigozie, Cole.
Chelsea XI confirmed!
And it's a strong team named by Alonso.
Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Chavarria; James, Barco; Estevao, Palmer, Rogers; Welbeck.
Subs: Sanchez, Anselmino, Hato, Watson, Lavia, Gittens, Neto, Emegha, Pedro.
Chelsea arrive at Stamford Bridge
Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro are all among the Chelsea players to arrive at Stamford Bridge. Is Xabi Alonso going strong?
Full team news will be confirmed shortly.
No VAR in operation
This stage of the Carabao Cup will not have VAR in operation. Something many will no doubt be grateful of.
The prize for tonight's winners
The third round draw has already been made. Bizarre, right?
But both sides this evening know that a home encounter against Leeds United awaits in the third round.
A hint at Chelsea changes
We should have confirmed team news soon enough but Alonso has said that Moises Caicedo and Marco Palestra are unavailable but goalkeeper Mike Penders might be given the nod between the posts. Wesley Fofana is suspended.
Welcome
Chelsea are not used to entering the Carabao Cup at this stage but after last season's disappointment, this will represent the first opportunity for Xabi Alonso to win some silverware.
Luton Town will view this as a free hit because few will expect them to progress no matter how many changes the Blues make.
Kick-off at Stamford Bridge is 19:30 BST.
new_text:
Danny Welbeck scored his first Chelsea goal as Xabi Alonso secured his first home victory as manager with a 2-0 win over Luton Town to set up a third-round Carabao Cup clash with rivals Leeds United.
Alonso named a strong side to face the League One outfit, selecting both Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, but it was the 36-year-old Welbeck who broke the deadlock early in the second half after Chelsea dominated the first.
The striker guided in Malo Gusto's cross to head in, before Estevao forced the second and Luton defender Hakeem Odoffin turned into his own net. Jamie Gittens hit the post late on after Rogers smacked the crossbar in the first half.
Chelsea's win came amid significant developments off the pitch, however. Manchester City remain in talks to sign Enzo Fernandez after the 25-year-old midfielder was left out of Alonso's squad to face Luton, while the Blues have agreed a £7.5m deal to sign Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez.
Follow live updates from Chelsea v Luton, below
Alonso on Fernandez move: Let's see how things develop
Asked whether he would like to keep Fernandez before the Luton match, Alonso added: "We want to have the best team possible. We know his qualities. He has shown it and we have to wait, but we will think about tomorrow and let's see how things develop."
Scott still a chance
The Independent understands Chelsea are prepared to go back to Bournemouth for midfielder Alex Scott after selling Fernandez. The Cherries have so far shut down any interest, but there's a belief a bid in excess of £80m, and probably closer to £90m, might bring reconsideration.
What Palmer has learnt from Alonso
Speaking to Sky, the Chelsea forward says of his new head coach: "He was a top player himself, so he's telling me little bits, what positions to pick up and especially before the game, to look at the opposition and where we can hurt them."
Enzo Fernandez in talks over £120m Man City move after absence from Chelsea squad
Manchester City remain in talks to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea after the 25-year-old midfielder was left out of Xabi Alonso's side to face Luton in the Carabao Cup.
Chelsea are holding out for a £120m fee for the Argentina international, which would make Fernandez City's record signing after the £116m fee they paid for Elliot Anderson this summer.
Sutton surveys Alonso's start
"Chelsea were always in control, Danny Welbeck with an excellent header for the first goal," the former striker says on BBC 5Live.
"Jack Wilshere will be mightily proud with the effort and the organisation which his team showed. It's another important win for Xabi Alonso, two from two.
"Leeds United will be a tougher test but they weren't really in much danger. They controlled the game and used the bench well. It's been a good start for Alonso.
"No European football for Chelsea so he knows how important it will be for him to try and win a trophy for Chelsea this season and if he can it will be a huge success but he has only just started."

Crystal Palace v Middlesbrough
Manchester United v Brighton
Manchester City v Norwich City
Sunderland v Hull City
Ipswich v Arsenal
Coventry v Aston Villa
Bournemouth v Lincoln

Chelsea v Leeds United

Everton v Wolves
Leyton Orient v Bradford City
Reading v Brentford
Peterborough v Barnsley
West Ham v Fulham
Up next
Alonso now turns his attention to Sunday's Premier League meeting at home to Brighton.
Wilshere will prep for Luton's trip to Mansfield.
Palmer named player of the match
Chelsea took 26 attempts on goal this evening.
Palmer struck eight.
He created another five.
Which goes a long way to explaining why he was named player of the match.
Palmer: 'We've had a look at ourselves'
"Last season wasn't good enough. We've had a look at ourselves. There's a new energy coming into the season. We'll keep pushing on. The gaffer has already said every game, every competition, we're there to win it."
